text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least one nuclear power reactor should be closed down, preferably before the next general election in September 1998, energy minister Anders Sundstrom says.
Opposition parties must accept this demand if they wish to take part in further negotiations regarding the future of the nuclear power programme, he stipulates.
- Health care in Sweden is no longer egalitarian. For the first time since 1970, people with low levels of education go less often to the doctor than people with higher educational qualifications.
- Although the paperwork can be a nightmare, Swedes can save tens of thousands of crowns by travelling to Germany to buy new and used cars.
- Interest in taking part in the Vasalopp, the world's largest cross-country ski race, is so great that a black market has emerged among skiiers willing to pay up to 750 crowns for a place.

- Labour market minister Margareta Winberg's idea of giving unemployed people jobs within the health care sector in a scheme funded by the labour market board is supported by Prime Minister Goran Persson.
- Beverage can maker PLM plans to invest heavily in Russia. The company is now in the final stages of talks relating to the construction of new plant in Moscow.

- Sweden's RIksbank is in the process of abandoning its two percent inflation target, professor Lars Jonung says. The central bank has expressed its intention both to keep to the inflation target and to bring the crown into the ERM. One of the two will have to go, Jonung says.

- Telecoms group Ericsson's third largest division Business Networks may be the company's new key growth area. Cordless communications using fixed networks for households and offices are an area that are expected to grow dramatically.
- Automotive group Volvo is to sign a deal on Thursday that is expected to lead to the construction of a new Indian truck factory.
- Spectacular share price gains for clothing retailer Hennes & Mauritz are just one indication of the stock market's renewed interest in consumer-related shares-
